cases.reasoning: Both are complete, usable procedures that retain the operating exceptions, ownership and safe closure requirements. A has a small usability advantage for a first-time closer: a standalone 'Lock up' section makes the last physical checks easier to find than B's combined handover-and-security section. This is a minor organizational preference, not a substantive difference in coverage.

expectations.text: Produces a 450–600 word procedure with the requested title, a 6:45 p.m. warning, the 7 p.m. transaction boundary, and two volunteers remaining through closure.
expectations.evidence: 572 whitespace-delimited words including headings. Title is 'Evening handover for the community tool library'; 'At 6:45 p.m., tell visitors'; 'At 7 p.m., let visitors already at the counter finish their current transaction. expectations.text: Gives actionable return checks, records observed missing parts/damage, quarantines visibly unsafe tools without testing or repair, and leaves disputed charges to the coordinator.

'Check the paper pickup list against the reservation screen'; retain existing name cards on the reservation shelf, 'Do not cancel reservations,' and log list mismatches.

expectations.text: Includes a witnessed cash count, dated and jointly initialed sheet, dated/totaled sealed envelope in the locked drawer, and records/escalates discrepancies without inventing a reconciliation policy.

'Seal the cash in an envelope marked with the date and total, then place it in the locked office drawer.' 'Send the coordinator the log link' only for dispute, cash or safety issues; next lead acknowledges at shift start. Lead checks cupboard/drawer; second volunteer checks back door; lead locks front and checks handle. 'If any door will not secure, stay together inside and call the building caretaker' using the entrance-wall number; do not leave unsecured.

expectations.text: Preserves the refrigerator/main-power exceptions and clear exits while excluding the log-merger story, lost draft, unreadable screenshot, stationery anecdote, and instruction embedded in the marginal note.
expectations.evidence: 'Keep exits clear'; 'Leave the refrigerator and the building's main power switch on.' Complete text contains none of the excluded production history or marginal instruction. It gives current shared-folder instructions directly.

strengths: Complete sequence from the warning through secured departure; standalone closing section supports first-time use.
Preserves easily lost operating conditions: no removal of equipment in use, borrower account/receipt contact, existing reservation cards, no new charges, no tool testing, and unresolved ownership.
All instructions are grounded in the notebook; no invented cash reconciliation rule.

cases.reasoning: Both preserve the full causal sequence, unsuccessful mitigation, impact and pending preventive work. B has a minor clarity advantage through useful cause/prevention headings and its explicit distinction between containment and correction: 'Pausing the worker contained the incident; it did not correct the concurrency flaw.' Its note that proposed monitoring is not an active control follows from the unresolved proposal. No factual or substantive quality difference warrants a stronger preference.

expectations.evidence: Title supplies '8 August'; 'Between 09:10 and 10:05 UTC, 312 accounts received one extra invoice notification. The ledger and invoices remained correct, and no account received an extra charge.' Reconciliation found no missed notifications; support contact completed at 11:40 with unchanged amounts/payment status.

cases.reasoning: Equivalent ready-to-use memos. Both lead with the same bounded recommendation and preserve the failed import/correction, actual trial uptake, phone workload, alternatives, cost, export uncertainty, unnamed administrator and quarter-end decision criteria. Neither overstates savings or comparative conflict rates. Small wording and placement differences do not materially change usefulness to program managers.

expectations.text: Recommends a one-quarter food-delivery-only Harbor pilot at $90 per month, leaving other programs on current calendars and requiring a named administrator, export rehearsal, and checked route mapping before launch.
expectations.evidence: Opening recommends 'a one-quarter pilot in the food-delivery program, conditional on a successful export rehearsal, a checked route mapping, and a named administrator before launch.' Other programs retain current calendars. Later: 'Harbor would cost $90 per month for this pilot, following a free trial.'

expectations.text: Retains the failed initial import affecting four volunteers, the inconsistent-route-name cause, its correction, and its relevance to migration readiness.
expectations.evidence: 'The first week's CSV import assigned four volunteers to the wrong route because the old route names were inconsistent.' Corrected mapping/re-import left no wrong-route assignment. 'Checking route mappings before the pilot is essential,' and maintenance is assigned to administrator's duties.

expectations.text: Accurately uses the 24-volunteer trial, 19 link users and five phone users without inventing why phone users did not use the link or claiming phone handling is eliminated.
expectations.evidence: '24 volunteers and two coordinators' in two weeks; 'Nineteen volunteers accepted at least one shift through the link. Five used phone calls, with a coordinator entering their shifts; the record does not explain their choice.' It explicitly says phone bookings and manual entry remained necessary.

expectations.text: Compares Harbor with the shared spreadsheet and separate calendars using their actual cost/conflict/reconciliation tradeoffs, without treating the two spreadsheet conflicts as a valid comparative rate.
expectations.evidence: Harbor provides a conflict view across two test routes at $90/month. Protected-column spreadsheet has no new subscription and permits phone bookings but requires manual checks. Its two conflicts in one week 'does not establish which approach has a lower conflict rate' without comparable Harbor measurements. Separate calendars avoid migration/subscription costs while retaining email reconciliation and no combined view.

expectations.text: Does not annualize the 11 observed reconciliation hours, claim measured Harbor time savings, assume proven export reversibility, invent an administrator, or supply unagreed numerical success thresholds; preserves the end-of-quarter stop/extend/expand review.
expectations.evidence: 11 combined hours in two weeks are 'not an estimate of annual savings'; trial did not measure time saved. CSV interface exists but 'reversibility has not yet been demonstrated'; rehearsal must rebuild schedules including phone-entered bookings. Director must name administrator; 'nobody has volunteered.' Quarter-end reviews time, conflicts, booking methods and administration to 'stop, extend, or expand'; numerical thresholds still require agreement, with no values invented.

summary.beyond_assertions: Checked the full outputs for omitted operating conditions, first-time-user usability, unsupported claims, sanitized failure history, invented phone-user motives, comparative rates and savings, unproven export reversibility, and changed owners/commitments. No additional material defect found. Case 305 B's inactive-monitoring warning is a supported implication; case 306's numerical-threshold wording does not invent a threshold.
summary.eval_feedback: Assertions cover the main risks well. Case 304's bundled return assertion does not individually enumerate equipment-in-use handling or directing disputed borrowers to receipt contact details; both outputs preserve these conditions, and they were checked beyond the assertion. No gap changes the verdicts.
summary.interpretation: The two minor preferences are local editorial judgments. Equivalent coverage and scores do not demonstrate overall superiority. No labels or source implementations were inferred.
